high_level_overview.overview: CBTRN02C is a batch COBOL program within the CardDemo credit card processing application, operating as a daily end-of-day transaction posting engine. It sits at a critical point in the payment processing workflow, responsible for moving validated daily transactions into permanent records and updating account balances accordingly. The program reads a sequential daily transaction file, validates each transaction against card cross-reference and account master data, and posts approved transactions to the permanent transaction file while routing rejected transactions to a separate rejects file. It solves the core business problem of ensuring only valid, within-limit, non-expired card transactions are permanently recorded and that account balances remain accurate and current.

key_features.description: Sequentially reads all transactions from the daily transaction input file (DALYTRAN) for processing.
Looks up each transaction's card number in the card-to-account cross-reference file (XREF) to confirm the card is recognized; rejects transactions with invalid card numbers.
Retrieves the associated account record to verify the account exists and is valid before allowing a transaction to post.
Calculates a projected balance including the new transaction amount and rejects any transaction that would cause the account to exceed its credit limit.
Compares the transaction origination timestamp against the account expiration date, rejecting transactions submitted after the account has expired.
Writes validated transactions to the permanent indexed transaction file (TRANSACT), capturing full transaction details including a DB2-formatted processing timestamp.
Updates the account master record with the new current balance and cycle-to-date credit or debit totals to reflect each posted transaction.
Maintains running balance totals by account, transaction type, and category in the TCATBAL file, creating new category records as needed.
Writes failed transactions along with a validation failure reason code and description to a daily rejects file for downstream review and reconciliation.
Displays total transactions processed and total rejections at job completion, and sets a non-zero return code if any rejections occurred to signal downstream job steps.

input_output.name: DALYTRAN-FILE
input_output.description: Daily transaction input file (DALYTRAN) - sequentially read to obtain each daily transaction record including transaction ID, type, category, amount, card number, merchant details, and timestamps for processing

input_output.name: XREF-FILE
input_output.description: Card cross-reference file (XREFFILE) - randomly accessed by card number to look up the associated customer ID and account ID for transaction validation

input_output.name: ACCOUNT-FILE
input_output.description: Account master file (ACCTFILE) - randomly read to validate credit limit, expiration date, and current balances; updated (rewritten) to reflect posted transaction amounts in current balance, cycle credit, and cycle debit fields

input_output.name: TCATBAL-FILE
input_output.description: Transaction category balance file (TCATBALF) - randomly read and updated to accumulate transaction amounts by account ID, transaction type code, and category code; new records are created if no matching key exists

input_output.name: TRANSACT-FILE
input_output.description: Transaction master file (TRANFILE) - indexed output file where validated and posted transaction records are written, including all transaction details and a processing timestamp

input_output.name: DALYREJS-FILE
input_output.description: Daily rejects file (DALYREJS) - sequential output file where failed/rejected transaction records are written along with a validation trailer containing the failure reason code and description

data_flow.description: Opens DALYTRAN (input sequential), TRANSACT (output indexed), XREF (input indexed), DALYREJS (output sequential), ACCOUNT (I-O indexed), and TCATBAL (I-O indexed) files. Any open failure causes immediate abend.
Sequentially reads the next record from the daily transaction input file (DALYTRAN) into DALYTRAN-RECORD. Sets END-OF-FILE flag to 'Y' on EOF, abends on any other read error.
Increments WS-TRANSACTION-COUNT for each record read. Resets validation failure reason and description to zero/spaces before validation begins.

Uses DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM as key to perform a random READ on the XREF-FILE (XREFFILE). If the card number is not found, sets WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON to 100 and description to 'INVALID CARD NUMBER FOUND'. On success, CARD-XREF-RECORD is populated including XREF-ACCT-ID.

data_flow.process: Validate Transaction - Account Lookup and Business Rules
data_flow.description: Uses XREF-ACCT-ID to perform a random READ on ACCOUNT-FILE. If not found, sets fail reason 101. If found, computes a temporary balance (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT - ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT + DALYTRAN-AMT) and checks against ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT (fail reason 102 if over limit). Also checks ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE against DALYTRAN-ORIG-TS (fail reason 103 if expired). ACCOUNT-RECORD is retained in memory for later update.
If WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON equals 0, the transaction proceeds to posting. Otherwise, WS-REJECT-COUNT is incremented and the transaction is written to the reject file.

For failed validations, copies DALYTRAN-RECORD into REJECT-TRAN-DATA and WS-VALIDATION-TRAILER (containing fail reason code and description) into VALIDATION-TRAILER. Writes the combined REJECT-RECORD to DALYREJS-FILE sequentially. Abends on write error.

Maps all DALYTRAN fields to the TRAN-RECORD structure (from CVTRA05Y). Calls Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP to generate a DB2-compatible processing timestamp from FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE and stores it in TRAN-PROC-TS.

Constructs a composite key from XREF-ACCT-ID, DALYTRAN-TYPE-CD, and DALYTRAN-CAT-CD. Attempts a random READ on TCATBAL-FILE. If the record does not exist (status '23'), initializes a new TRAN-CAT-BAL-RECORD, sets the key fields, adds DALYTRAN-AMT to TRAN-CAT-BAL, and WRITEs the new record. If the record exists, adds DALYTRAN-AMT to the existing TRAN-CAT-BAL and REWRITEs it. Abends on unexpected file errors.

Adds DALYTRAN-AMT to ACCT-CURR-BAL unconditionally. If DALYTRAN-AMT >= 0, also adds to ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT; otherwise adds to ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT. REWRITEs the updated ACCOUNT-RECORD back to ACCOUNT-FILE using the previously read record. Sets fail reason 109 if the rewrite key is not found.

data_flow.process: Write Posted Transaction to Transaction File
data_flow.description: Writes the fully populated TRAN-RECORD to the indexed TRANSACT-FILE (TRANFILE) using WRITE. Abends on any write error.

data_flow.process: Close All Files and Report Counts
data_flow.description: Closes all six files in sequence. Displays total transactions processed and total rejected. Sets RETURN-CODE to 4 if any rejections occurred, signaling a warning condition to the job scheduler.

data_dependencies.dependency: XREF Lookup Must Precede Account Lookup
data_dependencies.description: The account ID (XREF-ACCT-ID) used to key into ACCOUNT-FILE and TCATBAL-FILE is only available after a successful read of XREF-FILE using DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM. If the XREF lookup fails (reason code 100), the account lookup (step 1500-B) is skipped entirely via conditional branching.

data_dependencies.dependency: Account Record Must Be Read Before Update
data_dependencies.description: The ACCOUNT-RECORD populated during validation step 1500-B-LOOKUP-ACCT is reused directly in 2800-UPDATE-ACCOUNT-REC. No second read is performed before the REWRITE. This means the in-memory record from validation must remain unmodified between validation and posting, creating a strict sequential dependency between these two phases.

WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON acts as a gate. A non-zero value at the end of 1500-VALIDATE-TRAN unconditionally routes the transaction to the reject path (2500-WRITE-REJECT-REC) and bypasses all posting logic (2000-POST-TRANSACTION). This single field controls the entire transaction disposition.

data_dependencies.dependency: TCATBAL Record Existence Determines Write vs. Rewrite
data_dependencies.description: The WS-CREATE-TRANCAT-REC flag is set based on whether the TCATBAL READ returns status '23' (not found) or '00' (found). A WRITE is issued for new records and a REWRITE for existing ones. Issuing the wrong operation would cause a file status error and abend.

TRANSACT-FILE (TRANFILE) is opened with OPEN OUTPUT, which clears any existing content before writing. This means the program is designed for a full daily reload of the transaction file, not an incremental append. Running this program twice on the same day without regenerating DALYTRAN would result in data loss.

data_dependencies.dependency: Account Balance Computation Uses Cycle Credit/Debit Fields
data_dependencies.description: The overlimit check computes WS-TEMP-BAL as ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT minus ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT plus DALYTRAN-AMT. This depends on these cycle fields being accurately maintained. The subsequent 2800-UPDATE-ACCOUNT-REC also updates these same fields, so the correctness of future transactions within the same run depends on the accuracy of prior account updates within the same batch execution.

data_dependencies.dependency: Timestamp Generation Dependency on System Clock
data_dependencies.description: TRAN-PROC-TS is generated via FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE at posting time in Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP. All transactions posted in a single run will have timestamps reflecting actual wall-clock time at the moment of processing, not a single batch run timestamp. This creates a dependency on system clock accuracy and consistency.

The 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM paragraph calls the IBM Language Environment routine CEE3ABD with ABCODE=999 to force an abnormal termination. This is a hard dependency on the LE runtime being available in the execution environment. Without it, error handling for fatal file I/O failures cannot complete properly.

The program relies on CVTRA06Y for DALYTRAN-RECORD layout, CVTRA05Y for TRAN-RECORD layout, CVACT03Y for CARD-XREF-RECORD layout, CVACT01Y for ACCOUNT-RECORD layout, and CVTRA01Y for TRAN-CAT-BAL-RECORD layout. Field-level moves between file buffers and working storage records (e.g., DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM to FD-XREF-CARD-NUM) depend on exact length and type compatibility defined in these copybooks.

error_handling.description: Each of the six files (DALYTRAN, TRANSACT, XREF, DALYREJS, ACCOUNT, TCATBAL) has a dedicated open paragraph. After each OPEN, the file status is checked against '00'. If not successful, APPL-RESULT is set to 12, an error message is DISPLAYed identifying the specific file, the IO-STATUS is populated, 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS is performed to format and display the status code, and 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM is called to terminate the program abnormally.

Each of the six files has a dedicated close paragraph mirroring the open error handling. After each CLOSE, the file status is checked against '00'. Failures set APPL-RESULT to 12, display a file-specific error message, invoke 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS, and call 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM. A notable bug exists in 9300-DALYREJS-CLOSE where XREFFILE-STATUS is incorrectly moved to IO-STATUS instead of DALYREJS-STATUS.

In 1000-DALYTRAN-GET-NEXT, the sequential read checks for status '00' (success), '10' (EOF sets APPL-EOF/END-OF-FILE='Y' to gracefully end processing), or any other value (sets APPL-RESULT to 12, displays error, calls 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS and 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM). In 2700-UPDATE-TCATBAL, a READ on TCATBAL-FILE accepts both '00' and '23' (record not found) as valid, using the '23' case to trigger record creation via WS-CREATE-TRANCAT-REC flag.

Write operations in 2500-WRITE-REJECT-REC (DALYREJS), 2700-A-CREATE-TCATBAL-REC (TCATBAL WRITE), 2700-B-UPDATE-TCATBAL-REC (TCATBAL REWRITE), and 2900-WRITE-TRANSACTION-FILE (TRANSACT) all check file status for '00'. Failures set APPL-RESULT to 12, display a file-specific error message, invoke 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS, and call 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM to halt processing.

Business rule violations are handled as soft errors using a numeric reason code (WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON) and description (WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON-DESC). Code 100 = invalid card number (XREF lookup failure via INVALID KEY), Code 101 = account record not found, Code 102 = overlimit transaction (computed balance exceeds credit limit), Code 103 = transaction after account expiration. Any non-zero reason code routes the transaction to 2500-WRITE-REJECT-REC, increments WS-REJECT-COUNT, and writes the record with its failure reason to the DALYREJS reject file rather than aborting.

In 2800-UPDATE-ACCOUNT-REC, the REWRITE of the account record uses an INVALID KEY clause that sets WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON to 109 and WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON-DESC to 'ACCOUNT RECORD NOT FOUND'. However, this error is inconsistently handled — it sets the validation fields but does not write a reject record or abend, representing a gap in error handling since the transaction has already been partially posted at this stage.

9999-ABEND-PROGRAM is the centralized fatal error termination routine. It DISPLAYs 'ABENDING PROGRAM', sets TIMING to 0 and ABCODE to 999, then CALLs the IBM LE routine 'CEE3ABD' to force an abnormal termination with a user abend code, ensuring the job fails visibly and any dependent downstream jobs are not triggered.

9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS is a shared diagnostic routine called before every abend. It handles both standard two-character numeric file status codes and non-numeric or '9x' platform-specific status codes. For '9x' codes, it converts the second byte to a binary integer to extract the platform-specific reason code. The formatted four-digit status is displayed to the system log for operator diagnosis.

At normal end of processing, the program displays transaction and reject counts. If WS-REJECT-COUNT is greater than zero, RETURN-CODE is set to 4, providing a non-zero condition code to the JCL so downstream job steps or operators can detect that rejected transactions exist, without treating the run as a full failure.
